subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be for this request: a narrow `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, managed-proxy ownership, or a cross-tool fetch/search/browser policy with allow and deny semantics?
rationale: This creates an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while leaving deny/search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Design cross-tool policy first
options.body: Require a broader design covering fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, plugin HTTP, and deny semantics before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while leaving deny/search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This account owns the active scoped allowlist PR and has the strongest current routing signal for the SSRF/web-fetch boundary decision.
